HOPE BANCORP REPORTS FINANCIAL RESULTS FOR THE THIRD QUARTER AND NINE MONTHS ENDED SEPTEMBER 30, 2026
Third quarter 2026 net income grew 16% year-over-year and 8% quarter-over-quarter to $35.6 million
LOS ANGELES – October 28, 2026 – Hope Bancorp, Inc. (the “Company”) (NASDAQ: HOPE), the holding company of Bank of Hope (the “Bank”), today reported unaudited financial results for its third quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2026.
For the third quarter of 2026 , the Company reported net income of $35.6 million, or $0.28 per diluted common share, up 8% from net income of $33.0 million, or $0.26 per diluted common share, for the second quarter of 2026 , and up 16% from net income of $30.8 million, or $0.24 per diluted common share, for the third quarter of 2025. Excluding notable items, which consisted of merger-related costs, third quarter 2026 net income (1) was $37.5 million, or $0.29 per diluted common share (1) .
“Revenue growth and positive operating leverage drove strong quarter-over-quarter and year-over-year growth in pre-provision net revenue (1) and net income in the third quarter,” said Kevin S. Kim, Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer of the Company. “Through our continued focus on improving profitability, many key drivers contributed to this quarter’s results, including loan growth, lower deposit costs, net interest margin expansion, growth in customer fee income and disciplined expense management.”
Kim continued, “On October 1, 2026, we completed the acquisition of the Commercial Banking Unit of SMBC MANUBANK (“MANUBANK”), an important milestone in the continued evolution of Bank of Hope. The acquisition advances our core strategic priority to create long-term stockholder value by expanding our presence in Southern California, enhancing our deposit base, adding specialty deposit banking capabilities and broadening our ability to serve multinational customers with U.S. operations. Our Collaboration and Partnership Agreement with Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation (“SMBC”), which became effective upon closing, opened a meaningful channel to connect customers across markets. We warmly welcome the MANUBANK team and customers as we begin our next chapter together.”
“We remain focused on sustainable and profitable earnings growth across a range of operating environments, the results of which are demonstrated in our year-to-date earnings momentum. The strategic benefits of the MANUBANK acquisition will help bolster continued progress in 2027 and beyond,” concluded Kim. “We sincerely thank all our colleagues for their dedication and contributions to the ongoing integration process and the success of Bank of Hope.”
(1) Net income excluding notable items, earnings per diluted common share excluding notable items and pre-provision net revenue are non-GAAP financial measures. Quantitative reconciliations of the most directly comparable GAAP to non-GAAP financial measures are provided in the accompanying financial information on Table Pages 10 to 12. Notable items in the second quarter of 2026 included merger-related costs; notable items for the prior periods are detailed on Table Pages 10 to 12.
(more)
2-2-2 NASDAQ: HOPE
Operating Results for the Third Quarter of 2026
Net interest income and net interest margin. Net interest income totaled $135.4 million for the third quarter of 2026, up $6.4 million, or 5%, compared with $129.0 million for the second quarter of 2026, and up $8.8 million, or 7%, from the third quarter of 2025. Net interest margin for the third quarter of 2026 was 3.02%, up six basis points from 2.96% for the second quarter of 2026, and up 13 basis points from 2.89% for the year-ago quarter.
The sequential quarter increase in net interest income was primarily driven by growth in average earning asset balances, higher loan yields and lower deposit costs. The quarter-over-quarter net interest margin expansion was primarily attributable to higher earning asset yields and a favorable funding mix shift. The yield on average loans increased five basis points sequentially to 5.78% for the third quarter of 2026, while the cost of total deposits declined by two basis points to 2.58%.
Noninterest income. For the third quarter of 2026, noninterest income totaled $22.1 million, up $3.3 million, or 17%, compared with $18.9 million for the second quarter of 2026, and u p $6.7 million , or 44% , compared with noninterest income of $15.4 million for the third quarter of 2025. The sequential quarter increase in noninterest income reflects growth in customer-related income and fees and higher net gains on sales of Small Business Administration (“SBA”) loans, as well as $3.1 million in net gain on sales of other loans partially offset by a $1.2 million decrease in net gains on sales of securities available for sale. The Company sold $72.2 million of SBA loans in the third quarter of 2026 for a net gain of $4.7 million, compared with $67.9 million of SBA loans sold for a net gain of $4.4 million in the second quarter of 2026.
Noninterest expense. Noninterest expense for the third quarter of 2026 was $102.8 million, up $4.3 million, or 4%, from $98.5 million for the second quarter of 2026, and up $5.9 million, or 6%, from $96.9 million for the third quarter of 2025.
Noninterest expense excluding notable items (2) for the third quarter of 2026 was $100.1 million.
In the third quarter of 2026, the reported efficiency ratio improved to 65.3%, down from 66.6% in the prior quarter and 68.2% in the year-ago quarter, as revenue growth outpaced noninterest expense growth. This positive operating leverage also drove growth in pre-provision net revenue (2) , which totaled $54.7 million, up 11% quarter-over-quarter and 21% year-over-year. Excluding notable items (2) , the efficiency ratio for the third quarter of 2026 was 63.6%, and pre-provision net revenue (2) was $57.3 million.
Income tax provision and tax rate. For the third quarter of 2026, the Company recorded an income tax provision of $10.5 million, compared with an income tax provision of $9.6 million for the second quarter of 2026 and $5.6 million for the third quarter of 2025. The year-to-date effective tax rate for the first nine months of 2026 was 22.5%.
Balance Sheet Summary
Total assets. At September 30, 2026, total assets were $19.19 billion, compared with $18.99 billion at June 30, 2026, and $18.51 billion at September 30, 2025.
Loans . At September 30, 2026, gross loans totaled $15.12 billion, up 1% from $15.03 billion at June 30, 2026, and up 3% from $14.62 billion at September 30, 2025. Year-to-date, gross loans were up 2%. Third quarter 2026 average loans were $14.97 billion, up 1%, equivalent to 5% annualized, from $14.79 billion for the second quarter of 2026, and up 3% from $14.52 billion for the third quarter of 2025. Quarter-over-quarter, loan growth was primarily driven by increases in commercial and industrial and residential mortgage loans. Year-over-year, all of our major loan portfolios of commercial and industrial, residential mortgage and commercial real estate grew.

On a sequential quarter basis, end-of-period noninterest bearing demand deposits declined 1%; money market, interest bearing demand and savings deposits increased 10% in aggregate, and time deposits decreased 5%. The planned reduction in time deposits reflected our ongoing efforts to improve the funding mix and reduce the overall cost of funds. The share of time deposits in our deposit mix decreased to 36.7% at September 30, 2026, down from 39.9% a year ago.

Credit Quality and Allowance for Credit Losses
Criticized loans. Criticized loan balances remained essentially stable quarter-over-quarter and improved year-over-year. Criticized loans were $334.8 million at September 30, 2026, compared with $334.3 million at June 30, 2026, and down $38.1 million, or 10%, year-over-year from $372.9 million at September 30, 2025. The criticized loan ratio improved to 2.22% of total loans receivable at September 30, 2026, compared with 2.24% at June 30, 2026, and down 34 basis points from 2.56% at September 30, 2025.
Nonperforming assets. Nonperforming assets declined $4.4 million fr om the prior quarter to $108.5 million, or 0.57% of total assets, at September 30, 2026, compared with 0.59% of total assets at June 30, 2026, and 0.61% of total assets at September 30, 2025. The quarter-over-quarter improvement primarily reflected a reduction in nonaccrual loans.

During the third quarter of 2026, the Company continued to return capital to stockholders through its quarterly common stock dividend of 14 cents per share.
At September 30, 2026, total stockholders’ equity was $2.26 billion, compared with $2.30 billion at June 30, 2026, reflecting growth in retained earnings, return of capital to stockholders, and the net change in accumulated other comprehensive income (“AOCI”), which decreased due to the negative impact of rising interest rates on the fair value of available-for-sale securities. Book value per share at September 30, 2026, was $17.67, compared with $17.97 at June 30, 2026; and TCE per share (3) was $13.55 at September 30, 2026, compared with $13.85 at June 30, 2026.
Subsequent Events
Acquisition of SMBC MANUBANK Commercial Banking Unit . On October 1, 2026, the Company completed the acquisition of the Commercial Banking Unit of SMBC MANUBANK. As part of the closing of the MANUBANK transaction, the Company received an estimated (4) net cash settlement of $307.4 million from the seller, SMBC.
As of the acquisition date of October 1, 2026, loans acquired from MANUBANK totaled approximately $2.20 billion before purchase and other accounting adjustments, comprising $1.35 billion of real estate loans and $0.85 billion of commercial loans, which included $0.20 billion in SBA loans purchased by MANUBANK in the secondary market. Excluding these SBA loans, MANUBANK’s loan portfolio had a weighted average coupon rate of approximately 5.69% at October 1, 2026, before purchase and other accounting adjustments. MANUBANK’s SBA loan portfolio consisted of purchased guaranteed portions of 7(a) loans and these loans would have had a relatively low effective yield for the Company after acquisition; therefore, it was subsequently sold on October 21, 2026, for total net proceeds of $191.3 million with no gain or loss recognized on the sale.
Deposits acquired from MANUBANK totaled approximately $2.60 billion before purchase and other accounting adjustments, comprising $0.66 billion of noninterest bearing demand deposits, $1.77 billion of interest bearing non-maturity deposits, and $0.18 billion of time deposits. The acquired deposits had a weighted average cost of 2.22% at October 1, 2026, before purchase and other accounting adjustments.

Investor Conference Call
The Company previously announced that it will host an investor conference call on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, at 9:30 a.m. Pacific Time / 12:30 p.m. Eastern Time to review its unaudited financial results for its third quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2026. Investors and analysts are invited to access the conference call by dialing 866-235-9917 (domestic) or 412-902-4103 (international) and asking for the “Hope Bancorp Call.” A presentation to accompany the earnings call will be available at the Investor Relations section of Hope Bancorp’s website at www.ir-hopebancorp.com. Other interested parties are invited to listen to a live webcast of the call available at the Investor Relations section of Hope Bancorp’s website. After the live webcast, a replay will remain available at the Investor Relations section of Hope Bancorp’s website for at least one year. A telephonic replay of the call will be available at 855-669-9658 (domestic) or 412-317-0088 (international) for one week through November 4, 2026, with the replay access code 6995890.
